title: Feedback Orbit: catalog and probe notes
content:
TL;DR
A compact catalog of recurring customer asks (3 clusters) plus 6 low-effort probes we think can materially reduce friction and signal validity for product + serving runtime teams. Intended as a bridge doc for CS -> Eng spike planning this week (11/13). Not all asks are high priority revenue-wise; prioritization is cost-impact weighted (see matrix).

Context + approach
- Why this doc: multiple customers (mid-market and enterprise) reporting similar runtime and UX friction in the last 6 weeks; we pulled threads across support tickets, CSM notes, and a few joint-PO calls.
- Goal: synthesize signals into actionable micro-probes (<=2w engineering spikes or product experiments) and clear handoffs.
- What’s unique: we pair operational mitigations (e.g., routing/fallback) with customer-facing shadow-features (graceful degradations, suggested prompts) so impact is visible fast.

Signal clusters (high-level)
1) Burst latency variability during multi-turn chat (most frequent)
   - Manifestations: customers see 2-6x latency spikes mid-conversation with long histories; some attribute to KV cache misses and sequence length switching.
   - Representative quote: "Responses get super slow after a long back-and-forth — our users abandon the chat."
   - Common workaround in field: reduce history, use summarization hooks, or pin small context windows.

2) Cost unknowability when mixing embeddings and generation in a single flow
   - Manifestations: customers run composable pipelines (embed -> re-rank -> generate) and cost balloons unexpectedly. They ask for clearer per-route token+embed breakdowns and simulation tools.
   - Representative quote: "We couldn’t forecast our bill after enabling semantic search; we need a way to model cost before launch."

3) Silent degradation and mismatch between model variants
   - Manifestations: rollouts to quantized or smaller variants sometimes cause subtle hallucination regressions; teams notice but customers do not surface the signal cleanly.
   - Representative quote: "The answers changed after the update but still looked 'fine' — took hours to find."

Prioritization lens (quick)
- Criteria: customer impact (revenue/retention), engineering effort (spike vs. full product), unit-cost delta, time-to-visible-win.
- Quick ranking: Burst latency (P0 for one large customer + P1 for cluster), Cost modeling (P1), Silent degradation detection (P1-P2 depending on availability of eval hooks).

Micro-probes (actionable; estimated effort)
1) History-sensitivity thin-client (2w spike) — P0 for chat-heavy customers
   - What: an SDK-level opt-in that trims history intelligently (LRU by semantic similarity, not raw time) and exposes a single flag to applications.
   - Why: immediate latency wins, low infra change.
   - Acceptance: demo with synthetic convo showing 30–45% median latency improvement; one pilot customer (ACME Health) onboarded.
   - Linked artifact: JIRA ENG-4821 (spike).

2) Cost-simulator sandbox (3w product + small infra) — P1
   - What: a per-route cost simulator that given expected QPS and average tokens/embeds returns a monthly spend estimate and variance (scenarios).
   - Why: reduces pre-launch billing surprises and accelerates sales conversations.
   - Quick UI idea: route-level slider for batch sizing, quantization toggle, and expected unit cost preview.

3) Response-liveness telemetry flag (1w infra + 1w instrument) — P1
   - What: expose a lightweight metric capturing tail-latency per-customer-route segmented by sequence-length bracket and model-variant.
   - Why: helps SRE/product detect spikes and auto-notify impacted customers before CS does.

4) Probe: variant-diff smoke tests (1w) — P1
   - What: a nightly job that runs a small prompt set across the current and fallback model variants and surface semantic drift + token delta (not just log likelihood).
   - Why: catches silent quality regressions early.

5) Light-weight prompt-prescription playbook (1w writing + 1w CS rollout) — P0 for pilots
   - What: one-pager per common integration pattern with example prompts, ideal history window size, and routing hints (e.g., prefer base model for short Q/A).
   - Why: reduces self-remediation time for customers and reduces CS ticket volume.

6) Batch-aware default suggestions (2w) — P2
   - What: for routes using both embeddings and generation, show recommended batch/buffer settings and a sample cost impact preview.
   - Why: small UX change, can be toggled in Console per-route.

Customer vignettes (short)
- ACME Health (enterprise): chat latency spikes during long clinical note sessions. Impact: retention risk for trial users. Wants: immediate mitigation and SLA clarity.
- BrightFind (scale search startup): cost shock after adding reranker; asks for per-route spend preview and sandbox.
- NovelDocs (PMF stage): noticed answer quality shift after moving to 8-bit quant variant; concerned about subtle hallucinations.

Engineering notes / rough cost)
- History-sensitivity thin-client: mostly client + SDK changes; server accepts same payloads. Estimated 2 engineer-weeks (1 eng + 0.5 SRE).
- Cost-simulator sandbox: needs small modeling service + console UX; 3–4 engineer-weeks, ops review.
- Telemetry flag: piggyback on existing metrics pipeline; 1–2 engineer-weeks.
- Variant-diff smoke tests: reuse eval harness (already in research); 1 engineer-week.

Open questions / unknowns
- Do we have a safe canonical prompt set for multi-turn chat across verticals, or do we need per-customer seeds? (affects probe 4 scope).
- How much of the cost simulator value is self-serve vs. sales-assisted? (impacts UX surface).
- Risk: the history-trimming heuristic could degrade quality for retrieval-augmented setups; need a small safety net test (A/B small cohort).

Immediate next steps (owner + dates)
- 11/13: Sync (CS + Product + Serving Runtime) to pick 2 probes for the 2-week sprint. Owner: Aisha Patel.
- 11/14: Kickoff ticket for history-sensitivity thin-client, include ACME Health pilot details. Owner: Miguel Torres. (JIRA ENG-4821).
- 11/16: Console PM to prototype cost-simulator mockups. Owner: Sam Chen.

Appendix: quick patch-level playbook (notes to engs)
- If latency spike shows KV-cache misses: expose per-request headers to surface cache hit-rate to the caller; allow toggling of prefix caching for the route.
- For cost-surface: add per-embedding call metadata to billing logs (indexing key) so we can attribute embed usage by route.
- For variant-diff: use semantic similarity (embedding cosine) in addition to token- and log-prob deltas to flag changes.

Notes-to-self (CS style)
- Bring at least two customer examples to the 11/13 sync (ACME Health, BrightFind).
- Prioritize low-risk probes that give visible, exportable metrics for sales/CS.
- This doc will be iterated; add results of the first pilot as an update under "observations".
